Where it began

Sarfaraz Khan was born in Mumbai in 1997 and grew up in its suburbs, in a family from Azamgarh in Uttar Pradesh. Cricket came from home. His father, Naushad Khan, coached young players at Azad Maidan, and the boy spent much of his childhood there, learning to time the ball. When the monsoon made the trip to the maidan too hard, a synthetic pitch was laid beside the house so practice never stopped.

He made his name early. At 12, in his first Harris Shield match for Rizvi Springfield, he scored 439, beating a schools record that had belonged to Sachin Tendulkar since 1988.

The player

He went on to play two Under-19 World Cups, in 2014 and 2016, scoring heavily in both, and was, at 17, the youngest player the IPL had seen when he turned out for Royal Challengers Bangalore in 2015. In domestic cricket he played for Mumbai and Uttar Pradesh, and made a first-class triple century in January 2020.

His Test chance came in February 2024 against England at Rajkot, and he took it at a gallop. He made 62 from 66 balls in the first innings and 68 not out in the second, becoming only the fourth Indian with two fifties on Test debut, and India won by 434 runs, their biggest Test win by runs. By November 2026 he had played six Tests, making 371 runs at 37.10 with a hundred, a best of 150, and three fifties.

What made him special

He was an attacking middle-order batter, at his best against spin, quick on his feet and happy to play shots all round the wicket. On debut he and Yashasvi Jaiswal added 158 at more than six an over, at the time the quickest stand of 150 or more by an Indian pair in Tests.

His path to the Test side was not quick, and selection after his debut was not always regular. He kept turning up and kept scoring, which is the most any batter can do. In 2022 he even took the gloves from time to time in domestic T20 cricket, reviving a skill from his junior days.

Away from the middle

He was a member of the India side that won the Under-19 Asia Cup in 2013–14, and finished second in the run lists at the 2016 Under-19 World Cup, where India were runners-up. His early IPL innings won some famous admirers: after a 45 from 21 balls against Rajasthan Royals in 2015, Virat Kohli bowed to him as he walked off. He later played for Punjab Kings, Delhi Capitals and Chennai Super Kings.

And finally

Most of us were glad to make a few runs in a school match. Sarfaraz made 439 in one, which may explain why the rest of the cricket world has never seemed to rattle him much.
